name: Josh Allen
take: FantasyPros/CBS consensus have him as the undisputed dynasty SF QB1 (a tier alone), though age-30 keeps analysts at hold rather than aggressive buy.

name: Drake Maye
take: Clear QB riser after a QB2-caliber sophomore breakout; the A.J. Brown trade has FantasyPros/CBS calling him the next long-term dynasty QB1.

name: Jayden Daniels
take: A buy after an injury-derailed 2025; analysts still value his rushing profile as a Tier 2 anchor with league-winning upside.

name: Lamar Jackson
take: DLF flags his value as capped and a move-off candidate after an injury-riddled 2025 and a new Baltimore regime, though still a top-tier asset.

name: Joe Burrow
take: Analysts increasingly say trade-rather-than-hold given he's played 10-or-fewer games in two of three seasons, even as he stays elite.

name: Jalen Hurts
take: FantasyPros/CBS treat him as a Tier 2 core hold and elite point-producer despite a down year as a runner.

name: Caleb Williams
take: At 23 analysts favor him over Burrow on the mobility/age curve and tag him an ascending SF anchor, though some want more proof.

name: Jaxson Dart
take: Going ~QB9 in startups with QB1 upside, but the community is split over durability and a playstyle that invites injury.

name: Patrick Mahomes
take: CBS explicitly flags a sell at his lowest-ever ranking amid reduced rushing volume and Kelce's departure.

name: C.J. Stroud
take: DLF calls him a cheap buy-low at his lowest price point, betting on OC continuity after a down 2025.

name: Bo Nix
take: Analysts suggest moving off, citing 6.4 YPA and sub-4,000 yards on the most attempts — doubting he's a plus passer.

name: Cam Ward
take: Described as the market inefficiency right now — a sneaky buy as the No.1 pick with rushing upside.

name: Tua Tagovailoa
take: A buy-low value target as his price sinks, though Miami's coaching/offense uncertainty leaves analysts split.

name: Bijan Robinson
take: Consensus Tier 1 dynasty RB with no compelling reason to sell; interchangeable at the top with Gibbs.

name: Jahmyr Gibbs
take: CBS gives him the slight Tier 1 edge as overall RB1 on the better offense; a firm hold.

name: Ashton Jeanty
take: A buy-low after a rough rookie year on a bad Vegas offense — elite talent and a two-year age edge on peers.

name: Jonathan Taylor
take: CBS slots him ~RB5 as a proven, contract-secure hold, with age capping the elite window and some sell talk.

name: De'Von Achane
take: CBS lists him a sell despite RB4 upside, pointing to Miami coaching/QB volatility clouding the outlook.

name: Omarion Hampton
take: A year-2 breakout buy after an injury-shortened rookie year; analysts bullish on the new run scheme.

name: Quinshon Judkins
take: FantasyPros trade pieces say analysts are aggressively buying — exceptional rehab and a window if managers panic.

name: TreVeyon Henderson
take: Headwinds from a Patriots committee with Stevenson/Gibson; needs a year-2 leap and the community is split.

name: Bucky Irving
take: An undervalued buy-low at 23 as shoulder noise and the Gainwell add drop his price despite 14+ PPR/game.

name: Kyren Williams
take: Around RB21 as a stable but unexciting hold; no strong push, with lingering contract/committee questions.

name: Rhamondre Stevenson
take: Into the mid-RB30s as his value fades in a crowded New England committee alongside Henderson and Gibson.

name: Kimani Vidal
take: A cheap deep-league flyer gaining helium after leading the Chargers committee, but analysts split on his role behind Hampton.

name: Dylan Sampson
take: Around RB35 as a cheap dart-throw; analysts split on his path to touches, no strong consensus.

name: Ja'Marr Chase
take: Consensus dynasty WR1 who's never finished below WR11 in PPG, though analysts note JSN closing the gap.

name: Puka Nacua
take: Some analysts already have him WR1 as the NFL's all-time receiving-yards-per-game leader; an ascending elite hold.

name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
take: CBS says he's entered elite company as reigning OPOY; two years younger than Chase and could take over as dynasty WR1.

name: Malik Nabers
take: A buy on elite rookie production (WR6 PPG); analysts expect a top-five rebound returning from the ACL.

name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
take: About as consistent as it gets (WR3/WR4 PPG three straight years); a rock-solid hold.

name: Nico Collins
take: Around WR10, but recurring injuries and Stroud's play cap the ceiling, keeping opinions mixed.

name: Ladd McConkey
take: FantasyPros risers pieces show him gaining ground; analysts prefer him over Garrett Wilson on QB/environment.

name: Tee Higgins
take: Holds ~WR11/12 trade value as a steady producer, though age and sharing with Chase keep him a hold.

name: Garrett Wilson
take: FantasyPros notes sentiment has shifted — analysts worry he ages out of his prime before getting competent QB play.

name: George Pickens
take: Trade value has climbed (~WR18) in a new situation, but the community stays split on maturity and target security.

name: Jaylen Waddle
take: A solid but not elite hold; analysts flag Miami's offensive/QB uncertainty as the main drag.

name: Keon Coleman
take: Fallen to ~WR91 after a disappointing stretch; analysts divided on whether the cheap price is a buy.

name: Matthew Golden
take: Intriguing rookie-class talent in Green Bay, but analysts split given a crowded room and uncertain targets.

name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
take: A make-or-break buy-low: elite model score (No.2 behind Chase) clashing with two down seasons — analysts divided.

name: Brock Bowers
take: Unanimous dynasty TE1 with an elite ceiling and unmatched target potential; a premium hold.

name: Trey McBride
take: Consensus TE2 and elite hold, though analysts note Arizona changes could trim his volume.

name: Tyler Warren
take: Climbing into the TE2 tier with one of the highest TD ceilings among young TEs after a strong rookie year.

name: Colston Loveland
take: Rapidly closing the gap after a dominant finish; analysts group him with Warren as a cornerstone ascending TE.

name: Tucker Kraft
take: Rising on positive health reports into the top-five TE tier, though opinions still mixed on his ceiling.

name: Evan Engram
take: Largely dropped out of top dynasty TE tiers as age and a new situation fade his value — cheap contender depth only.
